This comic shop maintains an impressive graphic novel section that people who visit this comic shop consistently praise, with an extensive collection of trade paperbacks and graphic novels that cater to both casual readers and serious collectors, making it easy for customers to find complete story arcs and series in collected formats. The comic book store proudly carries a comprehensive selection of major publishers, with people who visit this comic shop specifically mentioning their extensive Marvel and DC offerings, including popular titles featuring Batman, Superman, and Spider-Man, while also noting the store's impressive collection of near-mint condition back issues of classic superhero series. How much do things cost here? Visitors consistently praise this comic shop's competitive pricing structure, with people who visit highlighting the incredible deals on back issues ranging from $1-4, affordable new releases, and special bargains in their used section that make collecting accessible without breaking the bank. How's the product selection here? People who visit this comic shop consistently rave about the store's vast and diverse selection, noting how well-organized everything is and appreciating how the inventory spans from the newest releases to hard-to-find back issues, with many mentioning they can always find what they're looking for thanks to the thoughtful organization by series and year. Collectibles & Action Figures This comic book store maintains a robust collectibles section that includes action figures, statues, and various other collectible items, with visitors noting the well-curated selection of figures that arrive well-packaged and are reasonably priced. Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More Based on local visitors, no one has mentioned finding Pokemon or Magic or Funko Pops products. The store carries an extensive manga and anime selection, with people who visit this comic shop specifically praising their manga box sets and comprehensive collection of Japanese comics. Is this place kid-friendly? People who visit this comic shop consistently note that this is a family-friendly establishment, with parents specifically praising the dedicated kids' corner and commenting on how welcoming the environment is for young readers, making it an ideal spot for introducing children to the world of comics.
summary: Near mint back issues sorted by series and year at $1 to $4 draw the collectors, while a dedicated kids' corner and manga box sets pull in the rest of the family.

name: Heroes
description:
Comic Book Store Details

Heroes located in Campbell, California, is described as one of the larger comic shops in the Bay Area, offering an extensive selection of comics in a welcoming space that combines old-school vibes with a well-organized layout, featuring everything from current issues to rare comics prominently displayed on the walls, though some visitors note the interior can be a bit dark.

This comic book store maintains an impressive collection of graphic novels, with multiple reviews highlighting their three full shelves dedicated to hardcover and trade paperback editions, ensuring readers have access to complete story arcs and collected editions.

Comic enthusiasts can find a diverse selection of Marvel and DC titles at this location, with multiple reviews specifically mentioning their extensive collection from both major publishers.

How much do things cost here?

According to visitors, pricing at this comic shop varies, with some finding the prices reasonable while others consider them on the higher end due to the Silicon Valley location, though the store offers various deals including a buy-2-get-1-free promotion and 10% discount for pull-list subscribers with 10 or more titles.

How's the product selection here?

People who visit this comic shop consistently praise the comprehensive selection, noting the store's extensive inventory of both new releases and back issues, with many highlighting how well-organized and easy to navigate the collection is, making it simple to find specific titles or discover new reads.

Collectibles & Action Figures

While this comic book store primarily focuses on comics, they do maintain a selection of collectibles and classic figurines, though reviews indicate the collection of toys and figures is not as extensive as their comic offerings.

Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More

Beyond comics, the store carries trading cards including Yu-Gi-Oh! cards, Pokemon cards, and Magic: The Gathering, adding variety to their inventory for collectors and gaming enthusiasts.

There are no specific mentions of anime, manga, or D&D products in the available reviews.

Is this place kid-friendly?

Based on the reviews, this comic book store appears welcoming to families, with one parent specifically mentioning their son's enjoyment of the Sonic the Hedgehog comic selection, though there aren't extensive comments about the child-friendly nature of the store.
summary: Three full shelves of hardcovers and trades anchor a dimly lit Bay Area shop known for rare comics displayed on the walls and a pull list discount that kicks in at ten titles.

name: Thunderdome Gaming
description:
Comic Book Store Details

Thunderdome Gaming located in Fort Pierce, Florida offers an old-school, treasure-hunt style shopping experience where visitors describe it as a cluttered but fascinating space filled with comics and collectibles in every nook and cranny, creating an environment that some find charming and others find overwhelming, with merchandise stacked from floor to ceiling in a way that makes browsing feel like an adventure of discovery.

While specific mentions of graphic novels are limited in customer feedback, people who visit this comic shop have noted the presence of various reading materials, including hardcover Marvel books, suggesting a diverse selection of comic-related literature throughout the store.

The store carries Marvel comics, as evidenced by mentions of hardcover Marvel books, though the exact extent of their superhero comic selection isn't clearly detailed in customer feedback.

How much do things cost here?

Customer feedback about pricing is mixed - while some visitors praise Captain Joel for being generous with deals and offering fair prices, especially for repeat customers, others mention inconsistent pricing practices and concerns about items being overpriced, with several noting that many items lack price tags and require asking the owner for pricing information.

How's the product selection here?

This comic shop boasts an extensive and eclectic selection that spans multiple categories, with visitors mentioning everything from board games to wrestling merchandise, though the organization of products tends to be described as chaotic and requiring patience to browse through.

Collectibles & Action Figures

The store features a wide array of collectibles and action figures, including Heroscape figures and various vintage toys, with customers describing the selection as extensive but requiring some dedication to dig through the various piles and boxes to find specific items.

Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More

While specific trading card games aren't prominently mentioned, the store appears to carry various gaming products.

The shop carries manga and board games, with visitors specifically noting the presence of these items among their diverse inventory.

Is this place kid-friendly?

Based on customer feedback about the cluttered nature of the store and tight spaces with precariously stacked merchandise, this might not be the most suitable environment for young children, though no specific mentions of child-friendliness are made in the reviews.
summary: Merchandise stacked floor to ceiling makes browsing feel like a dig, with Captain Joel cutting deals on Heroscape figures, vintage toys, and wrestling collectibles jammed into every corner.

description:

This comic shop maintains an impressive collection of trade paperbacks, with multiple visitors specifically highlighting the "mega tone" of trades available, making it an excellent destination for readers who prefer collected editions and complete story arcs.

While specific comic brands aren't explicitly mentioned in reviews, visitors consistently praise the comprehensive selection of comics available, suggesting a well-rounded inventory that caters to fans of all major publishers and characters.

How much do things cost here?

According to people who visit this comic shop, the pricing structure appears to be mixed - while many find the prices reasonable and competitive, some mention that wall books (presumably key issues and rare finds) tend to be priced on the higher side, though the store maintains an impressive selection of dollar comics for budget-conscious collectors.

How's the product selection here?

Visitors consistently rave about the extensive product selection, with many highlighting the impressive variety of back issues, including copper age comics and even some golden age western comics, while others appreciate the well-organized layout that makes it easy to find specific issues or discover hidden treasures among the vast inventory.

Collectibles & Action Figures

The store has earned a strong reputation for its collectibles section, featuring one-of-a-kind items like signed Kevin Smith comics, an impressive array of action figures, and what visitors describe as a "boggling selection" of statues, making it a must-visit destination for collectors seeking unique pieces to add to their collections.

Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More

Based on available reviews, the store offers some Pokemon-related merchandise, though specific details about trading card games are limited.

No specific mentions of anime, manga, or D&D products were found in the reviews.

Is this place kid-friendly?

While there aren't explicit mentions of child-friendly features, the store's community involvement through events like Free Comic Book Day and support of youth charities suggests a welcoming environment for readers of all ages.

This comic book shop shines in its collectibles selection, featuring an extensive array of miniatures for various tabletop games, Gundam model kits, gaming figures, and a particularly strong showing of D&D and Warhammer miniatures, with visitors frequently praising the variety and quality of these items.

The store carries Magic: The Gathering products and hosts Yu-Gi-Oh card game events, with visitors noting the availability of booster packs and pre-constructed decks.

Visitors consistently praise this comic shop's pricing structure, with multiple customers highlighting the exceptionally fair and competitive prices compared to other comic stores in the area, and while it's worth noting that the store operates on a cash-only basis, customers find the pricing so reasonable that they don't mind making a quick trip to the ATM.

How's the product selection here?

Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More

Based on customer feedback, this comic book store provides a welcoming environment for families, with staff taking special care to help parents find age-appropriate comics for young readers, as evidenced by one visitor's positive experience getting assistance selecting comics for their 5-year-old nephew.

description:

While specific mentions of graphic novels are limited in customer feedback, this comic book store appears to maintain a comprehensive selection of reading materials beyond single issues, with visitors noting the extensive variety of comics and printed materials available throughout the store.

The comic selection features both Marvel and DC titles mixed together alphabetically rather than separated by publisher, making it a more integrated browsing experience where people who visit this comic shop can explore titles across different universes in one continuous flow.

How much do things cost here?

People who visit this comic shop have mixed opinions about pricing - while some praise the fair values, especially for collectibles and vintage items, others mention prices running higher than online retailers, with the store maintaining a policy of 40% store credit and 30% cash for trades.

How's the product selection here?

The store boasts an impressively diverse inventory that visitors consistently praise, featuring everything from new weekly comic releases to vintage collectibles, with people who visit this comic shop often mentioning how they can spend hours exploring the densely packed aisles filled with comics, cards, and memorabilia.

Collectibles & Action Figures

This comic book store has earned a reputation as a collector's paradise, offering an extensive selection of vintage toys, action figures from various eras, movie memorabilia including horror franchises like Freddy Krueger and Pennywise, and various pop culture collectibles that span multiple decades.

Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More

Beyond comics, the store maintains robust selections of Pokémon cards, Magic: The Gathering products, and Funko Pops, with visitors frequently highlighting the extensive trading card game offerings.

name: Cryogenic Comics
description:
Comic Book Store Details
Cryogenic Comics is an up-and-coming destination for comic book fans in the Baltimore area. The shop is owned by Steve, who is passionate about finding and sharing great comics.

Every single comic in Cryogenic Comic's inventory is catalogued in an online database that you can view on your phone, tablet or computer. Call Steve at the number above if you want the database link or if you would like to schedule a time to visit Cryogenic's store in Catonsville.

Just ask and Steve will provide you with the house number the shop is located at.
How much do things cost here?
The issues at Cryogenic Comics range from 50 cents (coverless or poor condition) all the way to thousands of dollars each (valuable first appearances or rare issues). Read the product selection section for more details.

The sticker price for every priced comic is listed in the Cover Price field in Cryogenic's online database. The database also contains a list of all the issues that have not been priced in a separate tab.

Most of those issues are worth $5 or less, but it is possible to find an issue or two worth $10 or more. Steve will price any un-priced issue that you select as quickly and fairly as he can. Most of the time he'll look at the condition of the issue and quote a price. In some cases, he will look at sold ebay listings in order to determine a fair price for the same issue in similar condition. He will then price the issue lower than those sold prices.

When you buy 4 or more issues priced at $2 or more, you get a discount on your order. The discount is not a set percentage, the discount will increase as the total sticker price of your stack increases. The sticker price of their wall books (generally $70 or higher) is often negotiable. He WILL NOT raise the price of an issue right before you buy it! However, if the market price of an issue is much lower than the sticker price on the issue, Steve will do his best to lower the price to the current market value.
How's the product selection here?
They have a few Golden Age issues, but most are from the Silver Age to the current year.

They do not order brand new issues from distributors each week. Cryogenic's issues are all alphabetized and separated by price. There are 50 cent boxes, $1 boxes, $2 to $9 boxes, $10 and up boxes and then wall books that are priced at $70 and up.

Issues of a larger size like; graded comics, magazines and treasury sized issues are kept together. There's a box just for Spawn volume 1 ($2 to $60), a Deadpool box (most are $2) and a box with Rick & Morty ($3 to $4) and Simpsons ($4 to $35) comics.

They have a box packed with modern age books suitable for kids and another box with kids books that are older. There are also several CLOSED boxes of adult comics that are clearly marked.

Two boxes are priced and there are several short boxes that are not priced yet. They also have a short box filled with Underground issues that are for adults only.
Collectibles & Action Figures
They do not sell collectibles or action figures, however they have a tag in their database for comic issues that are based on toys such as G.I. Joe, Transformers and Masters of the Universe.
Trading Cards, Manga, Anime & More
Cryogenic Comics has a Manga tag in their database attached to any comic book that's of a Japanese manga or animé title. Aside from comic books and used comic book boxes, the only other item that they sell are hundreds of autographed 8x10 photos of actors and actresses. They are priced from $5 to $20 each. Steve can send you an inventory list of the actors he has in stock.
Is this place kid-friendly?
Yes. Since Cryogenic's shop is located in his home, any young customers should be accompanied by their parent or guardian. No ambient music is playing in the shop, so you don't need to worry about your kids hearing any adult language or lyrics.

Cryogenic Comics has boxes of issues just for kids and their adult boxes are closed, clearly labeled and are out of children's reach.
summary: Steve runs this out of his home, keeps every back issue catalogued in an online database, and has hundreds of autographed celebrity photos alongside the Silver Age bins.
